instruction: Open Chrome's settings page in a new tab.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated Thunderbird Bills folder, opened latest X/Twitter email, found link (help.twitter.com), right-clicked 'Open Link in Browser' to open in Chrome. The link timed out (ERR_TIMED_OUT) and model spent remaining turns retrying. Evaluator expected amazon.com in tabs but got help.twitter.com which was unreachable.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird folder tree, open/select emails, read email content, identify links, use right-click context menu 'Open Link in Browser', switch between apps, interact with Chrome tabs
metadata.failure_analysis: Model opened the wrong link (help.twitter.com from X/Twitter email instead of amazon.com from AWS email) and the URL was unreachable in the VM environment (ERR_TIMED_OUT). Model spent 12+ turns waiting and retrying the unreachable URL.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to Chrome-only navigation to an internal page (chrome://settings) which doesn't depend on external URL accessibility. Tests model's ability to open a new tab and navigate to a specific Chrome page.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening Chrome settings in a new tab. Evaluator uses is_expected_url_pattern_match to verify the active tab URL contains 'chrome://settings'.

llm_judge_reasons: URL pattern matching logic is correct: re.search('chrome://settings', result_url) will find a match even with the default 'https://' prefix prepended by the getter, since re.search checks for substring presence.
Getter get_active_url_from_accessTree correctly extracts the active tab URL from the accessibility tree and returns it as a string, which the metric handles properly.
Expected value is semantically correct: 'chrome://settings' is the correct URL pattern for Chrome's settings page.

Incomplete coverage: instruction says 'in a new tab' but evaluator only verifies the active tab URL matches chrome://settings. It does not verify that original tabs (apple.com, scholar.google.com) still exist, so navigating an existing tab to chrome://settings would also pass.
Config includes unnecessary Thunderbird setup (download, extract, launch) that is irrelevant to this Chrome-only task, though this does not affect evaluator correctness.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add a second evaluator step using is_expected_tabs or similar metric to verify that the original tabs (apple.com, scholar.google.com) still exist alongside the new settings tab, ensuring 'in a new tab' is verified.
Consider adding 'goto_prefix': '' in the getter config to avoid prepending 'https://' to chrome:// URLs, even though regex search still works with the double prefix.
Remove unnecessary Thunderbird config steps (download, extract, launch) since this task only involves Chrome.
